project.name: Create your own adventure
project.summary: A playable adventure REPL organized into Presentation, Application, Domain and Infrastructure; the executable wires the layers together.

nodes.label: Presentation
nodes.summary: Accepts player commands and displays tentative prose, accepted passages and save results.

nodes.label: Composition root
nodes.summary: Chooses concrete implementations and wires the four layers together.

nodes.label: Commands and signals
nodes.summary: Reads player intent and cancellation without reading ahead into later commands.

nodes.label: Story display
nodes.summary: Runs the play loop and drains prose and control output with bounded waits.

nodes.label: Application
nodes.summary: Owns accepted game state, explicit retry, autosave and shutdown decisions.

nodes.label: Story lifecycle
nodes.summary: Admits player intent and accepts completed generation only when it still belongs to the session.

nodes.label: Save policy
nodes.summary: Coordinates save attempts, load, recovery and final saving through replaceable execution contracts.

nodes.label: Execution contracts
nodes.summary: Defines cancellation, progress and background-work boundaries without terminal or vendor details.

nodes.label: Domain
nodes.summary: Keeps characters distinct and derives story memory, chapter continuity and rewind from accepted turns.

nodes.label: World and characters
nodes.summary: Validates worlds, protagonist selection and stable character identities while preserving namesakes.

nodes.label: Turns and memory
nodes.summary: Merges summary changes and derives chapters, recent prose and rewind from the turn log.

nodes.label: Settings and capabilities
nodes.summary: Defines checked text, limits, styles and the business capabilities for generation and saves.

nodes.label: Infrastructure
nodes.summary: Turns external model replies and saved documents into checked game values.

nodes.label: Story requests
nodes.summary: Renders bundled instructions and validates generated worlds, casts and turns.

nodes.label: Claude connection
nodes.summary: Checks subscription sign-in and accepts Claude structured results with optional narrative previews.

nodes.label: Codex connection
nodes.summary: Checks subscription sign-in and accepts one complete structured reply after successful cleanup.

nodes.label: Child process supervision
nodes.summary: Bounds process input, output, cancellation and cleanup for both storyteller connections.

nodes.label: Save documents and disk
nodes.summary: Validates saved games and supervises atomic primary and backup writes with explicit recovery.

nodes.label: Background execution
nodes.summary: Runs generation, storage and bounded blocking tasks behind application-owned contracts.

nodes.label: Checks and evidence tools
nodes.summary: Protects story behavior, boundaries, subprocess handling and disk recovery with tests and mutation checks.

nodes.label: Adventure rule tests
nodes.summary: Checks identity, summary merging, chapters and checked game construction.

nodes.label: Session policy tests
nodes.summary: Checks admission, retry, save policy and shutdown through controlled execution contracts.

nodes.label: Connection and disk tests
nodes.summary: Checks generated replies, process cleanup, library embedding and crash recovery.

nodes.label: Terminal acceptance tests
nodes.summary: Drives the shipped command through story, output, restart and shutdown cases.

nodes.label: Contract and mutation tools
nodes.summary: Runs registered behavior checks, dependency checks and deliberate regression probes.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.summary: Generates story content through the locally authenticated Claude CLI.

nodes.label: OpenAI Codex
nodes.summary: Generates story content through the locally authenticated Codex CLI.

nodes.label: Local save folder
nodes.summary: Keeps primary game documents, preceding backups and save-attempt evidence on local disk.

flows.title: Read the four layers
flows.description: These steps show compile-time dependency direction; the separate play/save flows show runtime work through ports.

steps.note: Presentation translates player input into application intent and renders read-only views.
Application owns canonical session and persistence policy through inward-owned execution contracts.
Domain owns checked game values, story rules and business capabilities.
The player submits a story direction.
The session admits one request and keeps the accepted game unchanged while work runs.
A background task runs the selected generation request.
Bundled instructions and checked response shapes guide generation.
When Codex is selected, one complete candidate is accepted after process cleanup.
Only a valid, current completion changes the canonical game.
The turn log determines updated memory and chapter context.
An accepted turn or rewind makes the canonical game need saving.
The storage runner preserves attempt identity while work runs.
A bounded helper validates and atomically writes the primary and backup.
The save folder retains the durable game and previous valid bytes.
A matching successful receipt marks the game clean; uncertainty remains explicit.

annotations.note: ARCH-001: canonical game ownership lives in the application; views expose no mutable game.
ARCH-003: keep each vendor tolerance adjustment local; shared schema and prompt generation stay vendor-independent.
ARCH-002: encoded save bytes stay private behind the application attempt handle.
